name: City Council Adjourned Regular Meeting of August 29, 2019
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 29, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:03 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (5:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 6:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 6:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 6:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.2.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:05 pm.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:04 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

5.  INVOCATION:  Mayor Quintero

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Quintero

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 29, 2019

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Mary Ann Powers – The budget is here and all we can say is God help us when you
  start looking at what monies are going out and what is coming in. I was just rather
  curious and I took a look at some of the disbursements that we have made according to
  City agendas since the first of the year and we used to have a Council person that drove
  us all nuts because he wanted to go line item by line item and it took so long but maybe
  we have to go back to that because as I was looking at the disbursements I saw from the
  City Attorney, Oversight Board $7,680 since January 1st and an Oversight Festival $440
  since January 1st what is that. I looked Oversight Board on the agenda and I saw
  Community Redevelopment and they haven’t had a meeting since June of 2018. What
  about wireless, what is wireless, are we paying for their telephones or are we paying for
  their wireless towers because we have paid over $50,000 since January 1st. Flair
  Spectrum Project $3,631.50 and that is on top of paying this group of attorneys
  $59,848.37 a month that is over $718,000 a year and we are worried about a helicopter
  program. This is crazy how much have we actually laid out and what is this money for?
  Is anybody asking? I think it is time. We paid out thousands of dollars for a freeway sign
  for Ross Nissan to the City Attorneys we could have bought the sign. We really need to
  take a look and people need to start taking a look at those disbursements and going
  back to asking questions even if it means we stay here until 11:00 and 12:00 o’clock at
  night. This is important and this is going to start cutting down on how we are spending
  our money.

  discussed, considered and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded

   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 29, 2019

14.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  14A.  Mayor Quintero

  I want to give a special thank you to SEIU, POA, PMMA and SEIU Mid
  Management they worked very hard with us. Both bargaining units or all the
  bargaining units did not have to speak to the City they were under no obligation.
  The POA had their contract until 2020 they could have said good luck City figure
  it out. Same thing with SEIU because of the me too clause it was believed that
  they could have gone on to 2020 without having to address any of the issues that
  we had but all of them said you need help we are there for you we are going to
  help work this out and because of their hard work it has made it at least a little
  easier for us to be able to move forward for the next few years and we are
  grateful to them for that and actually in the long term it is a much better deal for
  all those involved and we are so grateful for them for their leadership. I also want
  to specially thank who was acting in the capacity of Assistant City Manager at the
  time now our City Manager who engaged in those conversations as well in a very
  deliberate and a very true way to make sure that we got to this place. I would say
  we could of, should have been presented with a balance budget a couple of
  months ago but under the leadership of the City Manager now and the hard work
  of all the Department Heads and everyone involved they were able to get to the
  place where we needed to get to. It is going to continue to be a work in progress
  and we are counting on the Fiscal Oversight Committee to be able to continue to
  work with the Council completely to make sure that we continue to monitor and
  make adjustments along the way so that we are in a much better place within the
  next two years. So having said that I want to thank you all very much and wish
  you a wonderful evening.

  14B.  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco

  I would like to just quickly remind everyone that yesterday we had our Census
  meeting we had over 100 people, we hosted the San Gabriel Region. It is
  billions and billions of dollars it is $675 billion dollars of Federal funding that is
  going to be available to the cities that basically count. The residents, everyone is
  eligible to be counted regardless of where you come from. This is just money for
  the cities, for the schools for everyone so make sure that your cities. There is
  going to be employment for people that want to work during the Census so there
  are flyers out there. The other item is that I am also on the Mosquito and Vector
  Control and we meet once a month at 7:00 am and we are trying to find out what
  is going on with the infestation of mosquitos. The cities already contacted the
  organization they are going to work together to also work with the elders and
  work with the people that cannot get to their backyards to make sure that they
  are emptying out those buckets of water that are there that have been stagnant
  and abandoned pools. Flyers are out there.

  14C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  14C.1 Discussion Regarding Ban on Sale of Tobacco-Flavored Products.

  I brought an item to the attention of City staff. Less than a week ago the
  L.A. Times published an article on a possible ban on sales of flavored
  tobacco for e-cigarettes that can be coming to L.A. County it is actually
  being considered by our Board of Supervisors. This comes after health
  officials are calling the use of e-cigarettes by children it is becoming an
  increasing epidemic use amongst our teenagers. I would like to consider
  if this is the will of the Council to consider an ordinance on a ban of
  flavored tobacco for e-cigarettes in the City of El Monte. I think that this
  would be a great step in continuing to protect the health of our youth the
  use of nicotine at young ages when their brains are developing really has
  lasting and damaging effects so being that the Board of Supervisors are
  taking a good look at this and it might be coming to their agenda next
  month and it may be approved, I would like for us to consider as well
  reviewing what it would look like and possibly passing it as an ordinance
  here. I know that we need to do our research but I would like to instruct
  staff to move forward to bring to us in the future.

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 29, 2019

  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco – I would like to add support of it. I was just
  recently appointed to the County Commission on Alcohol and other Drugs
  Commission and that was one of the first meetings that I attended and it
  was brought up. It is a big problem, it is out of control, it is affecting a lot
  of kids and a lot of people and people didn’t think it was going to be
  affecting them so much but they are just popping out all over the place
  and we have heard in the news about kids dying. The County did give a
  thorough report to the Commission and they spent thousands of dollars
  going through it and the Commission recommended to start banning them
  but the cities can also do a lot. I would be more than happy to share the
  information that the County has provided to the public. Yes I am in favor
  of this.

  Councilmember Ancona – Part of the issue is that our youth doesn’t know
  that these e-cigarette products that they are consuming have nicotine.
  They just think that it just taste like watermelon or strawberry and they
  unfortunately don’t realize the damage that they are causing to their
  health, to their lungs, to their brain as they are developing.

  Mayor Quintero – There are some papers out now that just the vaping
  alone is causing damage to their lungs and that is still not known
  absolutely. Is there any objection to directing staff to review the possibility
  of an ordinance on this?

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Day One Pasadena Alisha Lopez is
  very familiar and has done a lot of work with a lot of cities with regards to
  resolutions so instead of us creating the wheel they have already got
  documents and templates so staff if you could reach out we are very good
  friends with Alisha Lopez and they can lead us in a quicker manner to
  getting something back to the table much sooner than if we were having
  to concoct something ourselves.

  Councilmember Ancona – I’ve actually forwarded something to Madam
  City Manager Martinez I have another document that I need to share with
  her so I will forward this along.

  Mayor Quintero – Thank you very much, thank you for bringing this issue
  to our attention no objection staff is so directed.

14D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Happy birthday Councilwoman Ancona we didn’t get a chance to celebrate you
  but I hope it was a good celebration another year on this earth another circle
  around the sun. For those of you who know and love her it is a blessing to have
  her in this community, here on this dais here in our life. This Monday is Labor
  Day, it is not just another day where we are just sitting down barbequing it is a
  time to reflect on all of those who are working so hard for us. Every single day
  my parents where in unions, my husband in unions and there are so many of our
  families that count on the support of the union to support them and to provide
  them with whatever it is that they’ve got on their minds with a living wage, with
  better hours with whatever it is that is on their minds with regards to their working
  environments. So on Monday I just want to say there is so much work that gets
  done that we are not conscious to and that we don’t ever say thank you to so
  today I am saying thank you to all of those who labor day in and out for the
  betterment of this City for the betterment of the community and for the betterment
  of our Nation. Thank you very much and have a safe and enjoyable Labor Day.
  Thank you.

14E.  Councilwoman Morales

  I wanted to mention that earlier today we had the skate park community outreach
  meeting and unfortunately there was a schedule conflict with today’s meeting so
  we would not be able to attend. However, our understanding is that it was highly
  visited and we had some very important visitors who were proving their input and
  that was the skateboarders themselves the teens in our communities they

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 29, 2019

  brought along their skateboards and they were providing us their input as far as
  the design that they would like to see incorporated into the skate park so we are
  really happy that those who are going to be using the park were absolutely
  represented and their input was documented so just wanted to that unfortunately
  we could not make it but nonetheless we are definitely taking their input into
  consideration with respect to the design and again reiterating the fact that we
  are working in collaboration with the Tony Hawk Foundation for grant funding to
  be able to have this park ready for our community teens and also to perhaps
  include some programming involved in there as well. So again apologies for not
  being able to make it but nonetheless it was highly supported by those who are
  going to be using it. Thank you.

  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco – I also wanted to thank Councilwoman Morales for
  taking the lead on this. I know you have been bringing in contacts and I wish you
  the best to bring in all the people you want to bring in.

  Councilmember Morales – In addition to the Tony Hawk Foundation we have
  been talking to other skateboard brands that are highly interested in providing
  programing making sure that the park is highly utilized and that the appropriate
  helmets, the appropriate knee pads and all the equipment that is necessary will
  be provided to children in our community free at cost.

 15.  ADJOURNMENT:

  With no objection Mayor Quintero adjourned the City Council meeting at 7:47 p.m.
